scope: Milestone C on-device verification of the Android companion client's command bar: the fixed key row (navigation keys plus Ctrl chords) and the snippet row below the stage, exercised live on the phone's cover screen through the ADB loopback harness. Finish line per spec: ^C verifiably interrupts a running program (exercised, not assumed) and snippets round-trip across process death.

checks.interrupt: send 'busy' through the composer, wait for the program's numbered output, swipe the key row until the ^C chip is on screen, tap it; the PTY line discipline turns the byte into SIGINT and the program reports 'busy interrupted after N lines'; the agent then answers a follow-up line, proving the session is alive after the interrupt
checks.snippets: open the editor (+ chip when the list is empty; long-press on the always-visible first chip once snippets persist), type a snippet, Add, Done; the chip appears in the bar with the saved text and tapping it sends paste+Enter (the fake agent echoes the line); force-stop and plain relaunch restores the chip from DataStore with the right text
checks.settings_toggle: the Settings switch's one device-visible effect, on a plain launch with no command-bar override so nothing masks the stored setting: verify the switch reports on and the stage shows the bar, hide it through Settings and verify the stage opens without the bar, then restore on so a failed run cannot leave the device stored-off; the restore's own failure verdicts are split — probe-shaped problems (the dump never established the switch) may ride under a SKIPPED only when the body passed, while effect-shaped ones (the switch did not flip, Done never returned, the raise) fail the run

defects_found_and_fixed: The snippet editor's test tags never reached uiautomator: AlertDialog opens its own window, so the root-level testTagsAsResourceId set in MainActivity does not apply to the dialog's composition, and the harness could not address any node inside it by resource id (the dialog itself opened and worked). Fixed by setting testTagsAsResourceId on the editor column and the Done button inside the dialog.

The busy workload first ran denser (a line every 150 ms) and uiautomator could not dump the window at all — the phone-side observation channel goes blind on a window redrawing that fast, which surfaced as a false 'the busy program never started' while the program was actually running. Slowed to one line per 1.5 s so dumps have quiet windows; the interrupt itself was always delivered.

The scrollback check left the terminal surrendered from follow-bottom (a drag landed off the live row), so later checks could not see new output. The check now scrolls back down to the live bottom before finishing and fails loudly ('scrolling never returned to the live bottom') if the prompt is not the last visible row.

PR review round found eight more issues, all fixed together: snippet bounds were enforced only at load, not at edit or save (now one SnippetStore.normalize projection shared by the bar, the editor, save, and reload, with an invariant test); DataStore threw IOException/CorruptionException into Main-dispatcher coroutines where UserDefaults is best-effort (the Settings seam now absorbs read and write failures for every key); commandBarEnabled/snippets state, the editor-open flag, and the editor's uncommitted rows and draft used plain remember so a fold recreation dropped them (rememberSaveable throughout, the row list via an explicit listSaver); the wide FlowRow had no vertical spacing and long snippet chips could wrap and grow the bar (verticalArrangement plus one-line ellipsized chips); the interrupt check leaked a running busy program on failure paths (try/finally best-effort ^C); the snippets check reused text across runs so a stale chip could satisfy the assertion (run-unique text) and assumed an empty editor (clears existing rows first); chip padding sat outside the click modifier so the visible chip border was dead to touches (padding now inside the clickable); and saved settings applied after first composition so a session opened at default geometry then resized (fit() gated on settingsLoaded).

A fifth review round (6 findings): both scrollback loops were vacuous — the accessibility text is a scroll-independent concatenation of history plus live frame, so the old text markers passed without verifying any movement. The terminal's contentDescription now leads with the follow state as a spoken sentence ("Following live output." / "Reading earlier output."), derived from the same followBottom that governs re-anchoring, so TalkBack announces whether the reader is at the live bottom and the harness anchors both loops on it. Chasing the newly-honest check exposed a real interaction hole: the composer submit leaves the on-screen keyboard open, the stage's imePadding shrinks the terminal to the strip above it (measured 746 px of viewport with the keyboard up, 1757 px with it down), and screen-center scroll gestures landed on the keyboard and never reached the list — the harness now drops the keyboard before scrolling (dismiss_ime, BACK gated on a dumpsys visibility check so it can never navigate out of the stage). Also fixed: the interrupt recovery branch tapped the ^C chip without re-revealing it (off-screen taps are silently dropped; it re-reveals first), the settings load could overwrite a toggle made during the load window (skip-once-loaded gate plus a Switch disabled until the read lands), the editor's length guard counted raw input while commit trims (guards and visible counters now count the trimmed form), and chord() accepted any Char while the arithmetic only holds for A..Z (require guard). One finding was rebutted empirically and pinned as a test: plain autoSaver preserves empty lists; the null-for-empty drop is specific to the library's builder savers.

A sixth review round (6 findings, all small): DataStoreSettings carried a dead CorruptionException catch after the IOException catch that already subsumes it (collapsed with a hierarchy note, both accessors); the settings load gate was rememberSaveable, restored to true on recreation where it would re-enable the Switch before the fresh read lands (plain remember, matching AgentStage's settingsLoaded); reveal() swipes in one direction and could latch the chip past the row's left edge, after which the containment test can never pass again (an overshoot now swipes back toward the row start); the best-effort interrupt cleanup caught only DeviceError while adb surfaces subprocess.TimeoutExpired and OSError (catches Exception); and this receipt double-counted two fixes across round bullets and described only the + chip path to the editor (deduplicated; both paths recorded above). Separately, a failed full-suite re-run traced to a stale --keep gateway still owning the fixture port: the readiness probe was answered by the old fixture, the phone drove its agents while the Mac observer watched this run's silent ones, and every Mac-side check failed against the wrong session — fixture() now checks the spawned gateway's liveness before the probe's success can return, so the run refuses to validate against a port it does not own.

A fourth review round (13 findings, all addressed): reveal() judged chip containment against wm-size panel width, which can report the unfolded panel while the cover display is in use, and swiped a fixed row height instead of the chip's own row (now judged against the command-bar node's own right edge and swiped at the chip's own vertical center, returning None when the bar itself is absent so callers name that failure); a failed interrupt left the busy program owning the PTY so the background and snippets checks failed with messages blaming the wrong interaction (a wedged flag now makes later PTY-typing checks report SKIPPED, recorded in the receipt, and fake_agent treats a stray ^C at the idle prompt as a no-op so the harness's best-effort second ^C cannot kill the fixture); the snippets check opened the editor through the + chip, which is off-screen once any snippet persists (the always-visible first chip's long-press opens the same editor); a second attached adb device could silently steal the run (--serial is now mandatory with more than one device); settingsLoaded was set only on the success path so an unexpected throwable in the reads would leave a stage that never opens (set in finally — opening at default geometry beats never opening); the settings effect keyed on fontSizeOverride so a debug-intent change re-ran the store loads and could revert a snippet save still in flight (keyed on settings, override read via rememberUpdatedState); setSnippets was a fresh unstable lambda each composition defeating CommandBar skippability (remembered like onInput); the settings toggle was flippable during the one frame before the DataStore read landed, which could write the default over a saved off (Switch disabled until commandBarLoaded); the editor rejected over-length pastes with no visible feedback (monospace n / 512 counters under each field); and the evidence receipt described commits and runs in prose (now explicit SHAs and commands).

Rounds 7 through 12 hardened the harness itself and pinned its probes: the device lock guard and the receipt writer's parsing branches gained unit tests (dbffc55, bedfdf3), the canned-device test double used by those tests was tightened to the real dump shape (1fc507e), and round 12 fixed the snippets check's editor-row seeding, made the terminal's spoken state sentence authoritative for the harness, and reclassified when a check may report SKIPPED (84bb4b4).

The settings toggle became a first-class device check: harness launches force the command bar on through the debug extra (6355678), the extra went three-state so the toggle check's plain launch neutralizes it and honors the store (5c4e406), and successive rounds hardened both halves — the probe polls for the switch's enabled flag before tapping (a tap on the disabled control is a silent no-op), refuses to tap without a reported checked state so it can never invert an already-correct switch (95ada98), and the restore-to-on cleanup stopped discarding its own failures, carrying them into the receipt instead (87fb62c, 1eacb44, e882fd2).

The fixture's busy program had a nested-interrupt hole: after a real ^C it prints a numbered report, and the harness's best-effort cleanup ^C could land while that report was still being written, killing the fixture's own reporting code. Four rounds contained it — ignore a second SIGINT while the report writes, bound that ignore window to the write itself so a wedged report stays interruptible, keep a raising handler everywhere else, and contain the nested handling at the report site instead of the process (aa3b14c, 67268bb, f4456e3, a1f0a2f).

Two late findings about the app's first composition: a launch with the bar disabled could open the session at default geometry and then resize once the bar's layout landed, so the stage now holds its first open until the measured bar visibility matches the configured one, with a two-frame escape hatch so a future bar layout that leaves the box height unchanged cannot hold the open forever (72b2cb8, d768d27); and the snippet list could be reverted by a store read racing an in-flight save across a fold recreation — the load now applies once (saveable flag), the commit makes the live list authoritative, and the editor cannot open against the pre-load placeholder, where Done would commit the empty seed over the stored list (d768d27).
limitations: Ctrl chords other than ^C (^D ^U ^L ^R ^Z ^W) are unit-tested as raw control-byte payloads but not individually exercised on device; ^C is the spec's named finish line and its SIGINT path through the PTY is the same wire shape all chords use.
The compact-width scrollable strip is what the cover screen exercises; the expanded FlowRow layout at >=840dp awaits milestone D's unfolded-display gate, as does any posture-docked placement.

Snippet persistence is per-device DataStore; the settings toggle check verifies the stored on-state after a fresh launch and the off-state on stage re-entry within the same process, always restoring on — the off-state across process death is not a separate check row.

Transport remains the adb-reverse loopback with the fake_agent fixture; the tunnel is established once per run and the app deliberately does not auto-reconnect a dropped stream (it surfaces a manual reopen banner), so a mid-run transport loss does freeze that run's typing. The two failed runs (20260930-193605 and 20260930-233211) were first blamed on exactly that; their artifacts contradict it. Both ran with the phone's cover display rotated to landscape: 2520x1080 captures, the stage's own agent stream opening at 120x8 and 120x15 with the run's grid set 120x10/120x15/120x17/120x8/73x6 (73 columns is the resize check's 720x1600 override landing in a landscape window), while every green run today — including 20260930-225924 at the same product code — is portrait, 1080x2520 with 56x45 to 56x52 grids. The failure shape is posture, not transport: exactly the six typing checks fail while every non-typing check is green. The harness asserts no display posture, so a rotated phone reports six unexplained check failures instead of one named posture error; adding that precondition is candidate follow-up work, not part of this milestone. The real-Codex overlay run is still folded into the milestone A/D gates.
